speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe how this wound on your right lower leg started and how long it has been present? Also, have you noticed any changes in its appearance or size over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience pain or a heavy sensation in your legs that worsens when standing for long periods? Also, have you noticed any darkening or discoloration of the skin around the wound?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of chronic swelling, a prior DVT, and a family history strongly suggests venous insufficiency. To confirm this, I will look for signs of venous stasis changes like hyperpigmentation or lipodermatosclerosis around the wound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Ankle-Brachial Index rules out significant arterial disease, which supports a diagnosis of chronic venous insufficiency. I will now examine the wound edges and surrounding skin for specific signs like hemosiderin staining or induration.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prior DVT and family history, this is likely post-thrombotic syndrome. Do you notice any weeping or exudate from the wound, and is the surrounding skin hard or indurated?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of diabetes and fever makes infectious or neuropathic etiologies less likely, further supporting a venous origin. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous stasis ulcer
